name: London
tagline: World Financial Center, West End Theatre, and Centuries of Living History
description: London is one of the world's great cities — a global financial capital with unmatched theater, world-class museums, and a dizzying diversity of cuisine and culture. The NHS provides universal healthcare, and the city's public transit system is among the best on earth. However, London is brutally expensive for housing and dining, making it a challenging FIRE destination unless your portfolio is substantial.

quickFacts.visa: 6-month visitor visa for US citizens. No dedicated retirement visa — long-term options are limited for retirees. Investor visa requires £2M+ investment. Most retirees cycle tourist visas or explore ancestry routes.
quickFacts.safetyRating: Moderate — generally safe but petty crime exists in crowded tourist areas
quickFacts.nearestAirport: Heathrow Airport (LHR) — 45 min from central London; also Gatwick (LGW), City (LCY), Stansted (STN)
quickFacts.climate: Temperate maritime with cool summers (18-23°C) and mild winters (3-8°C). Frequent overcast skies and drizzle year-round.

housing.description: Small studio or 1-bedroom in Zone 3–4 (Walthamstow, Lewisham, Tooting fringe, Croydon border)

dining.description: A few inexpensive meals out; mostly home cooking

transportation.description: Oyster PAYG / partial Zone 1–3 Travelcard; no car (London transit is genuinely expensive)

1M.lifestyle: A small studio or one-bedroom in Zone 3–4 — Walthamstow, Lewisham, or the Tooting fringe — with an Oyster/Travelcard covering the Tube and buses and no car. NHS access comes via the Immigration Health Surcharge, so health cost is low, and most meals are cooked at home with the odd pub or market meal. London's transit and council tax push the everyday floor higher than most cities, so dining out is constrained, but the free museums, the parks, and the whole city within Tube reach keep life full.

housing.description: Comfortable 1-bedroom in Zone 3 or the Zone 2–3 fringe

healthcare.description: IHS plus a basic private top-up (entry Bupa/AXA)

2M.lifestyle: A comfortable one-bedroom in Zone 3 or the Zone 2–3 fringe, with a full Zone 1–3 Travelcard and regular casual dining. A basic private layer joins the NHS/IHS base for faster specialist access, and there is room for cinema, occasional theatre, and a gym. Central-ish London living without the prime-postcode premium.

housing.description: Quality 1-bedroom in Zone 2–3 (Clapham, Islington/Hackney fringe, Greenwich)

dining.description: Regular dining including some mid-range dinners

transportation.description: Zone 1–3 Travelcard plus occasional Uber/black cab

3M.lifestyle: A quality one-bedroom in Zone 2–3 — Clapham, the Islington/Hackney fringe, or Greenwich. Dining out is regular, comprehensive private cover (Bupa/AXA) sits on top of NHS access, and the Travelcard plus occasional Uber or black cab cover the city. Mid-tier gym, theatre, and concerts are routine, with genuine margin — affluent London life without a car, in one of the world's great cities.

housing.description: High-end 1–2 bedroom in Kensington, the Chelsea fringe, Marylebone, or Notting Hill

healthcare.description: IHS plus a premium private plan

transportation.description: Zone 1–6 Travelcard plus frequent cabs and a car-club (first tier a car appears — discretionary)

5M.lifestyle: A high-end one- or two-bedroom in Kensington, the Chelsea fringe, Marylebone, or Notting Hill, with a weekly housekeeper. Dining is frequent and fine, a premium private plan removes friction, and a Zone 1–6 Travelcard plus frequent cabs and a car-club membership cover transport. A premium gym, opera and theatre, and club memberships fill out prime-London living.

housing.description: Grand flat or townhouse in Belgravia, Knightsbridge, or Mayfair, or a Hyde Park penthouse

healthcare.description: IHS plus concierge / Harley Street private care

entertainment.description: Private members' clubs (Annabel's/Soho House), premium culture

domesticHelp.description: Housekeeper several times a week (~50 hrs/mo @ ~£21.5/hr, central premium)

10M.lifestyle: A grand flat or townhouse in Belgravia, Knightsbridge, or Mayfair, or a Hyde Park penthouse, kept by a housekeeper several times a week. Dining runs near-daily at Michelin tables, health cover pairs NHS access with concierge Harley Street private care, and a part-time chauffeur and car handle evenings. The discretionary budget funds private members' clubs, premium culture, art and wine, and constant travel. London is the priciest market here by a wide margin, so even this budget is anchored by super-prime housing — but daily life is at the top of what the city offers.
